_comment: The same single-file shape as named-seam-single-file.json, except the import is aliased: the module exports `evaluateGate` and the file binds it as `gate`, which is the name the findings use. Both spellings have to count as naming what the module provides, or a real seam reads as a guess.

findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the decision atomic with what is pushed**

The verdict is taken before the lock is held, so a concurrent writer can change what the call sends after it was judged.

The call into `gate` is where this has to hold. Nothing revalidates it, so the race stands.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revalidate the ref along with the revision**

The revision is compared but the ref is not, so a concurrent writer pointing another ref at the same revision passes `gate` unchanged. Nothing revalidates it, so the race stands.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Judge the identity that was captured**

The reads still follow ambient state rather than the identity captured up front, so the verdict can describe something the call will not send.

The call into `gate` is where this has to hold. A concurrent writer wins the race unless this is revalidated.
